slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 22:8: Abraham answered, ‘God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.’
slides.body: “Abraham answered, ‘God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.’”
slides.heading: Gen 22:8

slides.alt_text: Slide 2: Did God promise Jesus as the lamb? Abraham tells Isaac that God will provide a lamb. A ram is then killed instead of Isaac. John later calls Jesus “the Lamb of God.”
slides.body: Abraham tells Isaac that God will provide a lamb. A ram is then killed instead of Isaac. John later calls Jesus “the Lamb of God.”
slides.heading: Did God promise Jesus as the lamb?

slides.alt_text: Slide 3: Why Christians connect them A beloved son faces death, but God provides another victim in his place. Christians see this as a powerful preview of God giving Jesus to save others.
slides.body: A beloved son faces death, but God provides another victim in his place. Christians see this as a powerful preview of God giving Jesus to save others.
slides.heading: Why Christians connect them

slides.alt_text: Slide 4: But the story gives its own answer God provides a ram for that day’s sacrifice. John never says he is referring to Isaac’s story, and his lamb image could come from several other Bible passages.
slides.body: God provides a ram for that day’s sacrifice. John never says he is referring to Isaac’s story, and his lamb image could come from several other Bible passages.
slides.heading: But the story gives its own answer

title: Did Abraham promise Jesus as God's lamb?
